my_indicator_label: state peak demand and peak demand not met (CEA, August 2026)
literature_closest_variable: National and state coincident peak electric demand (GW) and loss-of-load probability (pdf p. 1, ROW-0170; pdf p. 3, ROW-0174; E07 p. 16, ROW-0104)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature reports macro all-India peak forecasts (388 GW by FY32) and Virginia peak forecasts (60 GW), but does not report district-level or monthly peak deficits for Indian states [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Peak demand figures mix diverse non-coincident industrial loads; data centre baseload is flat (load factor >0.85) unlike weather-sensitive residential summer peaks [I].

my_indicator_label: energy not supplied (%)
literature_closest_variable: Loss of load probability (LOLP) and grid frequency excursion duration above statutory ceiling (pdf p. 10, ROW-0119; pdf p. 20, ROW-0153, ROW-0154)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature tracks system-level frequency excursions (50.39 Hz events in Aug 2024) and generation LOLP, but does not provide distribution-level unserved energy by district [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Energy not supplied at DISCOM level reflects distribution transformer failures, whereas data centre grid impacts manifest as transmission thermal overloads and frequency deviations [I].

my_indicator_label: rural and urban hours of power supply (state, FY 2023-24)
literature_closest_variable: Continuous 24/7 power supply requirements (pdf p. 12, ROW-0127) vs residential feeder reliability (pdf p. 1, ROW-0178)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Sources quantify that data centres require uninterrupted 24/7 power (E08 pdf p. 12, ROW-0127) and extreme spatial load concentration (Ireland DCs exceeding all urban homes, E16 pdf p. 1, ROW-0178), but do not publish rural/urban feeder supply hours [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Feeder supply hours reflect agricultural rationing and DISCOM power procurement scheduling, not physical substation presence of data centres [I].

my_indicator_label: serving DISCOM and its 14th Integrated Rating grade
literature_closest_variable: DISCOM financial stress, fixed-cost socialization, and cross-subsidy surcharge erosion from open access (pdf p. 14, ROW-0131; pdf p. 70, ROW-0102; pdf p. 19, ROW-0110, ROW-0111)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature analyzes DISCOM commercial revenue erosion from large loads using open access, but does not correlate utility credit ratings with data centre penetration [I].
suggested_caveat_I: A poorly rated DISCOM (e.g. Grade C/D) faces severe borrowing cost penalties when financing dedicated 220 kV substation upgrades demanded by data centre developers [I].

my_indicator_label: transmission company (STU / InSTS)
literature_closest_variable: Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) and Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) capacity additions and regional transfer bottlenecks (pdf p. 2, ROW-0171, ROW-0172)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature reports national aggregate InSTS lines under construction (30,387 ckm, 118,194 MVA), but does not break down nodal transformer headroom by STU [I].
suggested_caveat_I: STU boundary defines transmission wheeling charges and intra-state open access regulations, which CEEW (E08) identifies as the primary regulatory friction point [I].

my_indicator_label: grid-constraint evidence by district
literature_closest_variable: Substation-by-substation capacity bottlenecks, transmission corridor saturation, and transformer lead times (pdf p. 15, ROW-0134; pdf p. 14, ROW-0150; pdf p. 1, WEB-0016; pdf p. 3, WEB-0020)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Sources document specific corridor bottlenecks (Kalwa/Padghe in Mumbai, Eastern Loudoun in Virginia), but lack comprehensive district-level grid constraint registers across all Indian states [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Grid constraints are hyper-local: a district may have surplus generation 100 km away but face local 220/33 kV transformation deficits [I].

my_indicator_label: live and planned data centre MW per district (IT load and facility load kept separate)
literature_closest_variable: Operational MW vs pipeline MW, rack power density (kW/rack), and IT load vs facility power via PUE (pdf p. 2, ROW-0059; pdf p. 45, ROW-0096, ROW-0097; pdf p. 12, ROW-0146; pdf p. 2, WEB-0021)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature provides city-level operational totals (Mumbai 53%, 1,700 MW India total), but does not break down live vs planned MW by administrative district [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Crucial to enforce PUE multiplier: an IT load of 100 MW translates to 120-140 MW facility grid demand depending on cooling technology [I].

my_indicator_label: planned MW as a share of state peak (ranking only, because it mixes stages)
literature_closest_variable: Data centre peak demand as a share of utility / regional coincident peak (pdf p. 6, ROW-0085; pdf p. 23, ROW-0114; pdf p. 1, ROW-0170)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature calculates utility peak shares (Dominion 25% peak, Ireland 23% metered), but warns against mixing speculative queue requests with operational load [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Rankings are valid for identifying state-level grid exposure, but summing announced pipeline MW directly overstates immediate grid impact due to 50%+ drop-out rates [I].

my_indicator_label: state data centre renewable rules (open access, banking, cross-subsidy surcharge)
literature_closest_variable: Dual sourcing, open access regulatory friction, banking restrictions, and mandatory on-site clean dispatchable rules (pdf p. 14, ROW-0130; pdf p. 20, ROW-0138; pdf p. 4, ROW-0160; pdf p. 3, WEB-0014)
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Literature documents broad state policy levers and Ireland's mandatory 80% PPA rule, but does not provide a cross-state clause-by-clause comparison of Indian banking charges [I].
suggested_caveat_I: State open access rules dictate commercial viability: banking restrictions force developers to oversize solar/wind systems or install expensive BESS [I].

indicator_id: INDICATORS IN THE SOURCES THAT I DO NOT HAVE
my_indicator_label: Crucial power and grid variables identified in the literature absent from district dataset
definition_and_importance
literature_closest_variable: source_reference

my_indicator_label: The ratio between nominal contracted substation capacity (MVA) and actual operational metered draw (MW). Sources show developers contract 2x their actual metered load.
measured_same_way_I: Compare DISCOM sanctioned load agreements against actual 15-minute billing demand data from SLDC [I].
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Reveals true physical grid impact and prevents over-allocation of scarce transmission capacity [I].

indicator_id: Interconnection Queue Drop-out and Speculative Multi-Queuing Rate
my_indicator_label: The percentage of grid connection requests that represent duplicate applications across adjacent substations rather than committed capital.
measured_same_way_I: Track attrition rate between Stage-I connectivity approval and Stage-II operationalization in STU filings [I].
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Essential for distinguishing speculative real-estate pipeline from genuine electrical demand [I].

indicator_id: Operational Load Factor and Power Factor
my_indicator_label: Data centres operate with exceptionally flat load factors (>0.85) and near-unity power factors (0.95-0.99) behind active front-end UPS systems.
measured_same_way_I: Sample hourly feeder SCADA telemetry at dedicated data centre substations [I].
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Differentiates continuous industrial baseload from peaky residential demand in generation planning [I].

indicator_id: Substation Transformer Spare Headroom (N-1 Contingency MVA)
my_indicator_label: Firm transformer transformation capacity remaining at 220/33 kV or 400/220 kV substations under single-contingency failure conditions.
measured_same_way_I: Calculate (Substation Rated MVA * 0.8) minus Coincident Peak MVA from STU annual reports [I].
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Identifies exact physical nodes where new large data centre connections will trigger grid failure [I].

indicator_id: On-Site BESS and Captive Generation Ride-Through Duration
my_indicator_label: The duration (minutes/hours) that on-site battery storage or diesel gensets can sustain facility load during grid voltage sags or peak evening ramps.
measured_same_way_I: Inspect state pollution control board (SPCB) diesel generator permits and CEIG electrical safety filings [I].
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Determines facility capability to provide demand curtailment and avoid tripping local grid [I].

indicator_id: QUESTIONS THE LITERATURE SUGGESTS ASKING OF EACH INDIAN STATE
my_indicator_label: Targeted empirical and regulatory questions grounded directly in literature findings
focal_hub
literature_closest_variable: core_inquiry_question
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: pdf_page

my_indicator_label: Mumbai / Navi Mumbai
literature_closest_variable: E09 documents that 2-3 GW of concentrated data centre load sits on the Kalwa/Padghe corridor into Mumbai, which hosts 53% of national capacity (pdf p. 8, ROW-0143; pdf p. 14, ROW-0150). E08 highlights peri-urban clustering in Navi Mumbai (pdf p. 19, ROW-0136).
pdf_page: What is MSETCL's firm N-1 transformation headroom at 400/220 kV substations feeding Airoli, Mahape, and Chandivali, and what volume of captive BESS is mandated for new connections?
measured_same_way_I: Substation MVA headroom and captive BESS ride-through duration
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Determine whether Mumbai's transmission corridor can absorb committed IT load without causing cascading blackout risks [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Thermal overload of transmission corridors feeding islanded urban grids [I]

my_indicator_label: Visakhapatnam
literature_closest_variable: E09 and E12 report Google's 1 GW hub and 6 GW of total data centre commitments in Visakhapatnam (pdf p. 3, ROW-0140; pdf p. 2, WEB-0013). E06/E07 highlight severe ratepayer stranding risks from large load exits (pdf p. 10, ROW-0093; pdf p. 19, ROW-0110).
pdf_page: Under APERC's draft Resource Adequacy regulations, what credit collateral and minimum connection duration terms are imposed on hyperscale developers to protect APEPDCL from stranded asset recovery?
measured_same_way_I: Contracted minimum take-or-pay duration and developer financial bank guarantee terms
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Prevent agricultural and residential consumers from absorbing multi-billion-rupee fixed grid expansion capex if projects downsize [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Utility balance sheet insolvency and residential tariff spikes [I]

my_indicator_label: Hyderabad
literature_closest_variable: E09 operational data demonstrates August 2024 frequency spikes reaching 50.39 Hz during solar surplus (pdf p. 20, ROW-0153, ROW-0154), while E08 notes data centres require uninterrupted 24/7 power (pdf p. 12, ROW-0127).
pdf_page: How will TSSPDCL and TSTRANSCO manage midday solar over-generation if data centre baseload remains static, and is mandatory demand-ramping or BESS absorption being introduced?
measured_same_way_I: Dynamic demand-response tariff structures and daytime solar absorption mandates
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Assess whether Hyderabad data centres can serve as flexible sinks for state solar surpluses or if they worsen grid instability [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Cascading grid frequency collapse and tripping of double-conversion UPS systems [I]

my_indicator_label: Chennai (Ambattur / Siruseri)
literature_closest_variable: E09 notes double-conversion UPS rectifiers generate low-order harmonics (5th, 7th, 11th) and lack dynamic models (pdf p. 12, ROW-0148; pdf p. 10, ROW-0157), while E10_P1 and E18 show Ireland mandated FRT compliance to prevent transient blackout risks (pdf p. 4, ROW-0159; pdf p. 2, WEB-0027).
pdf_page: Does TANTRANSCO enforce mandatory Fault Ride-Through (FRT) and dynamic load simulation modeling for hyperscale facilities connecting to coastal 400 kV substations?
measured_same_way_I: Mandatory FRT Grid Code clauses and dynamic load modeling standards
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: Ensure large electronic loads do not disconnect simultaneously during coastal transmission line faults, risking regional grid collapse [I].
suggested_caveat_I: System-wide voltage collapse caused by simultaneous 'silent exits' of large converter loads [I]

my_indicator_label: National / State Interface
literature_closest_variable: E06 documents that Dominion builds transmission to serve 1,000 MW metered load when customers request 2,000 MW capacity (pdf p. 69, ROW-0101). E02 notes tracking interconnection queues risks overestimation due to projects in multiple queues (pdf p. 8, ROW-0029). E15 reports Dominion's contracted queue reached 53.8 GW in July 2026, as reported by a secondary source (pdf p. 2, WEB-0022).
pdf_page: What is the actual empirical divergence between state data centre policy MoU announcements (MW) and executed, fee-paid STU grid connection agreements?
measured_same_way_I: Ratio of announced policy pipeline MW to physically executed STU Stage-II connection agreements
what_literature_cannot_tell_me: De-bias data centre growth projections from speculative developer press releases and political investment summits [I].
suggested_caveat_I: Overbuilding transmission infrastructure based on phantom paper demand [I]
